# 1 Load

## 1.1 Libraries of functions: 

I uploaded data and packages of necessary functions to perform the calculations, and set the working directory.

```{r, setup, results=FALSE, include=FALSE, echo = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning=FALSE)
package_to_load <- c("readxl", "readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "tidyr", "dplyr","RColorBrewer", "car")
for (package in package_to_load) {
  require(package, character.only = T); packageVersion(package)
}
extra_to_load <- c("knitr","stringr", "stringi", "ggrepel","ggpubr", "ggbreak","reshape2")
for (package in extra_to_load) {
  require(package, character.only = T); packageVersion(package)
}
#rm(package_to_load, microb_p_to_load, extra_to_load)
```

I load the mouse model Ribotag CPM data.


# 2. Exploration of the data

## 2.1 Fe's metabolism gene list

This is the table where there is the list of genes of interest (second column). I observed there are 64 rows but 62 unique genes because Pcbp1 and Pcbp2 participate in 2 different pathways.
```{r, echo = FALSE}
print(paste("Genes:",dim(genes_list)[1],"; and parameters:",dim(genes_list)[2])) # 64 genes and 7 parameters
# str(df) # Too large
#print(paste("Table of gene symbols:",table(genes_list$Symbol)))
kable(head(genes_list[1:6,]),format = "simple", caption = "Section of gene list associated to Fe metabolism.") #%>% kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")%>%column_spec(1, bold = T)
```

## 2.2 Pre-process Ribotag's data

Exploration of the Raw Ribotag's data (normalized in CPMs):

```{r, echo = FALSE}
print(paste("Genes:",dim(df)[1],"; and samples and probes' columns:",dim(df)[2])) # 15355 genes and 17 samples (+1 column of the probe's Symbols)
kable(head(df[1:6,1:6]),format = "simple", caption = "Section of CPM's table from Ribotag's data") #%>% kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")%>%column_spec(1, bold = T)
```

Exploration of the metadata's related to Ribotag's data:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
print(paste("Samples:",dim(metadata)[1],"; and parameters:",dim(metadata)[2])) # 4 parameters and 17 samples
kable((metadata[,1:4]),format = "simple", caption = "Section of CPM's table from Ribotag's data") #%>% kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")%>%column_spec(1, bold = T)
```

# 3. Pre-processing

## 3.1 Presence of specific genes:

Definition of the list to check.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
a <- unique(genes_list$Symbol)
print(paste("Length of the gene list:", length(a),"genes")) # 62 genes
b <- as.data.frame(a)
```

Our aim is to obtain a new data frame for each data set, with the list of 62 genes associated to Fe's metabolism. If there are any gene not analyzed by the data set, we assign zero value to the genes.

## 3.2 Set the working table

There are 51 genes from the list in the table, but I proceed the table in order to integrate the genes not analyzed and I have assigned zero value to them:
```{r, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rownames(df) <- df$gene
colnames(b) <- 'gene'
df2 <- left_join(b, df, by="gene") # By joining this way, I keep the genes from the Fe metabolism not analyzed by Ribotag (NAs)
df2 <- df2[-which(is.na(df2$C48)==TRUE),] # I remove rows of genes associated to Fe's metabolism not analysed in Ribotags'
sum(is.na(df2)) # 0
df2 <- as.data.frame(df2)
print(paste("Dimensions of the table:",dim(df2)[1],"genes, and ", dim(df2)[2], "(1 probes' column + 17 samples)"))# 56 genes    18 (1 parameters + 17 samples)
kable(head(df2[1:6,1:6]),format = "simple", caption = "Section of Lam et al data associated to Fe metabolism.") #%>% kable_styling(full_width = F, position = "left")%>%column_spec(1, bold = T)
#List of Fe metabolism related genes not analyzed by Lam et al
#print("List of Fe metabolism related genes not analyzed by Lam et al:")
#names(which(colMeans(df2[4:ncol(df2)]) == 0)==TRUE)
```

# 4. Expression levels

Second, I need to explore the expression levels of those genes that are present.

## 4.1 Visualization

First, I explore the expression levels of all the available cells:

```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=6, echo = FALSE}
df3 <- as.data.frame(t(df2[,-1]))
colnames(df3) <- df2$gene
df3$Sample <- rownames(df3)
df3 <- left_join(metadata, df3, by= 'Sample')
rownames(df3) <- df3$Sample
library(reshape2)
df4 <- reshape2::melt(df3,id= c("Group","Sample","Diet","Time"))

ggplot(df4,aes(value, variable)) + geom_boxplot(aes(value, variable,fill=as.factor(variable)),alpha = 0.6)+geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Expression levels\n(CPM)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels both diets")+ theme(legend.position = "none")#+theme_classic()
library(ggridges)
ggplot(df4,aes(value, variable,fill=as.factor(variable))) + geom_density_ridges(aes(value,variable, fill=as.factor(variable)),alpha=0.6)+ 
  theme_ridges() + geom_point(color="gray7", alpha = 0.85)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Expression levels both diets\n(CPM)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels")+ theme(legend.position = "none")#+theme_classic()
```

Due to we considered different diet and time-course groups, I split the plots into facets. 
```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=6, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(df4,aes(value, variable)) + geom_boxplot(aes(value, variable,fill=as.factor(variable)),alpha = 0.6)+geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Expression levels\n(CPM)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels")+ theme(legend.position = "none")+facet_grid(Diet ~ Time)
library(ggridges)
ggplot(df4,aes(value, variable,fill=as.factor(variable))) + geom_density_ridges(aes(value,variable, fill=as.factor(variable)),alpha=0.6)+ 
  theme_ridges() + geom_point(color="gray7", alpha = 0.85)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Expression levels\n(CPM)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels")+ theme(legend.position = "none")+facet_grid(Diet ~ Time)
```

Thanks to this, I can observe clear changes in some genes in time such as Fth1 and Ftl1.

To improve this visualization, I reverse one of the facets and assign different colors to it:

```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=6, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(df4,aes(value, variable)) + geom_boxplot(aes(value, variable,fill=as.factor(Diet)),alpha = 0.6)+geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Expression levels\n(CPM)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels")+ theme(legend.position = "top")+facet_grid(. ~ Time)
#library(ggridges)
#ggplot(df4,aes(value, variable,fill=as.factor(Diet))) + geom_density_ridges(aes(value,variable, fill=as.factor(Diet)),alpha=0.6)+ 
#  theme_ridges() + geom_point(color="gray7", alpha = 0.85)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Expression levels\n(CPM)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels")+ theme(legend.position = "top")+facet_grid(. ~ Time)
```

## 4.2 Log2 visualization

First, I log2 transform the expression levels because I realized the expression levels' changes of genes that express higher levels may mask the changes of genes that express lower levels:

```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=6, echo = FALSE}
df4$Log2value <- log2(df4$value)

ggplot(df4,aes(Log2value, variable)) + geom_boxplot(aes(Log2value, variable,fill=as.factor(variable)),alpha = 0.6)+geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Scaled expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "none")#+theme_classic()
library(ggridges)
ggplot(df4,aes(Log2value, variable,fill=as.factor(variable))) + geom_density_ridges(aes(Log2value,variable, fill=as.factor(variable)),alpha=0.6)+ 
  theme_ridges() + geom_point(color="gray7", alpha = 0.85)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Scaled expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "none")#+theme_classic()
```

Due to we considered different diet and time-course groups, I split the plots into facets. 
```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=6, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(df4,aes(Log2value, variable)) + geom_boxplot(aes(Log2value, variable,fill=as.factor(variable)),alpha = 0.6)+geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Scaled expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "none")+facet_grid(Diet ~ Time)
library(ggridges)
ggplot(df4,aes(Log2value, variable,fill=as.factor(variable))) + geom_density_ridges(aes(Log2value,variable, fill=as.factor(variable)),alpha=0.6)+ 
  theme_ridges() + geom_point(color="gray7", alpha = 0.85)+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Scaled expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "none")+facet_grid(Diet ~ Time)
```

Thanks to this, I can observe clear changes in some genes in time such as Fth1 and Ftl1.

To improve this visualization, I reverse one of the facets and assign different colors to it:

```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=6, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(df4,aes(Log2value, variable)) + geom_boxplot(aes(Log2value, variable,fill=as.factor(Diet)),alpha = 0.6)+#geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+
  labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Scaled expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)",fill = "Diet") +ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "right")+facet_grid(. ~ Time)
library(ggridges)
ggplot(df4,aes(Log2value, variable,fill=as.factor(Diet))) + geom_density_ridges(aes(Log2value,variable, fill=as.factor(Diet)),alpha=0.6)+ 
  theme_ridges() + geom_point(color="gray7", alpha = 0.85)+
  labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Scaled expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)",fill = "Diet")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "right")+facet_grid(. ~ Time)
```

If I try to include another variable per gene, customize the colors and turn right the plot:

```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(df4,aes(variable,Log2value)) + geom_boxplot(aes(variable, Log2value,fill=as.factor(Diet),color=as.factor(Time)),alpha = 0.6)+#geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+
  labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Scaled expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)",fill = "Diet",color="Time") +ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "right",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1,vjust = 1))+ 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "tomato", "21" = "tomato4"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("CD" = "turquoise3", "HFD" = "gold3"))
```

If I also want to add statistics I need to split it again:
```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=11, echo=FALSE}
library(ggpubr)
g1 <- ggplot(df4,aes(variable,Log2value)) + geom_boxplot(aes(variable, Log2value,fill=as.factor(Diet),color=as.factor(Time)),alpha = 0.6)+#geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+
  labs(x="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",y="Expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)",fill = "Diet",color="Time") +ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "right",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1,vjust = 1))+ 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "tomato", "21" = "tomato4"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("CD" = "turquoise3", "HFD" = "gold3")) +
  #facet_grid(.~Diet)+

  #stat_compare_means(aes(group = Time))
  stat_compare_means(aes(group = Time),label = "p.signif", method = "t.test",hide.ns = TRUE)+
  stat_compare_means(aes(group = Time),label = "p.format", method = "t.test",hide.ns = TRUE, label.y = 12.5, size =2)

  #stat_compare_means(aes(group = Time),label = "p.signif", method = "t.test",ref.group = "0", label.x = 13)
g1
pdf(file = "Boxplots_Fe_associated_genes_Ribotag_P0P21_Timestatistics.pdf", width = 20, height = 11)
g1
dev.off()

g2 <- ggplot(df4,aes(variable,Log2value)) + geom_boxplot(aes(variable, Log2value,fill=as.factor(Diet),color=as.factor(Time)),alpha = 0.6)+#geom_point(color="gray4", alpha = 0.8)+
  labs(x="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",y="Expression levels\nlog2(CPMs)",fill = "Diet",color="Time") +ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nExpression levels after Log2 transformation")+ theme(legend.position = "right",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1,vjust = 1))+ 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "tomato", "21" = "tomato4"))+

  stat_compare_means(aes(group = Diet),label = "p.format", method = "t.test",hide.ns = TRUE, label.y = 12.5, size =2)
```

## 4.5 Log transformation FC

Due to it seems better to interpret, Sara suggested to visualize Chow diet data in fold changes of P21 vs P0:

```{r}
library(reshape2)
df3 <- df2 %>% 
  mutate(CD0_mean = rowMeans(df2[,2:6])) %>% 
  mutate(CD21_mean = rowMeans(df2[,7:9])) %>% 
  mutate(FC = CD21_mean/CD0_mean)

#Probes <- unique(df5$variable)
df6 <- df3[,c(1,21)]
df6$Log2_FC <- log2(df6$FC)
df6$FC_trend <- if_else(df6$Log2_FC > 0, "Up","Down")
#df6$gene <- reorder(df6$gene, df2$gene)
#df6$reference <- sapply(df6$gene, function(x) which(x == df2$gene))
df6 <- df6[order(match(df6$gene, Probes)),]
df6$Symbol <- df6$gene
df6 <- left_join(df6, genes_list, by = 'Symbol')

pdf(file = "Barplots_Fe_associated_genes_Ribotag_P0P21_Timestatistics_Log2FC_ChowDiet.pdf", width = 12, height = 15)

g1

g2 <- ggplot(df6,aes(Log2_FC, gene), order=as.factor(Pathway)) + geom_col(aes(Log2_FC, gene,fill = as.factor(FC_trend),alpha = 0.6, order=as.factor(Pathway)))+labs(y="Genes associated to the metabolism of Fe",x="Expression levels\nLog2(FC)")+ggtitle("Ribotag's P0 vs P21 data\nLog2 transformed Fold changes (P21 means/P0 means)")+ theme(legend.position = "none")+ scale_fill_manual(values = c("Up" = "tomato", "Down" = "deepskyblue1", "0" = "violet")) + facet_grid(Pathway~., scales = "free_y")
```
